description: The Use of Extreme Value Theory for Forecasting Long-Term Substation Maximum Electricity Demand is a data set deposited in IEEE DataPort by its authors Yun Li. This dataset contains daily maximum load data with the average demand, customer count and PV capacity at two substations Arkana and Muchea, Western Australia used in the accepted IEEE Transactions on Power Systemspaper titled “The Use of Extreme Value Theory for Forecasting Long-Term Substation Maximum Electricity Demand” by Li and Jones (2019). Coverage: national (AU); the metadata date the deposit to 2019. The formats are not stated in the metadata. It is reached through its DOI or landing page, listed on this page. Access is free of charge, and IEEE DataPort normally asks for a free account before download (not tested). The licence is Creative Commons Attribution. Caveats: written from the DataCite metadata (title, abstract, subjects and rights) read on 2026-09-29; the deposit itself was not opened or downloaded, so its contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support power-system, energy-planning and grid-operation studies. Related record: the repository-level record data-ieeedp-repository.
